summary: Autoscaling edge runners create short-lived sessions that fragment customer token buckets, causing recurring 429s for low-volume clients
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a dedicated pool (FjordData) are seeing recurring 429 responses for low-to-moderate traffic workloads after a recent autoscaling change at the edge. The pattern is: brief successful requests from a small fleet of workers followed by a cluster of 429s for the same API key even though aggregate token usage is well below tenant quota.

Impact:
- Several endpoints for FjordData return intermittent 429s for short periods (30–90s) across multiple client processes.
- Customer reports increased error rates in production while overall token consumption is unchanged.
- This affects webhooks and low-QPS inference jobs more than sustained high-throughput clients.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted, Dedicated pool: fjord-prod-01
- Region: us-west-2
- Components: edge-proxy (HTTP2 multiplexing), regional rate-limiter, autoscaler that spins up/down edge runners, tenant-level token-bucket accounting
- Recent change: edge autoscaler rollout v2.3.1 (shorter TTL for idle runners, faster scale-up)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a bursty job pattern: 10 short-lived worker processes that each make 1–3 requests and exit; repeat every 2 minutes.
2) Observe successful calls initially, then after several cycles, some requests begin returning 429s for a window ~30–90s.
3) If workers are kept long-lived (reuse connection/session), 429s do not appear.

Observed behavior:
- 429 responses include X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 and X-RateLimit-Reset showing a near-future timestamp.
- Edge proxy logs show many distinct ephemeral session IDs and short-lived connections mapped to the same API key.
-Regional rate-limiter metrics show multiple small token-bucket debits that do not aggregate cleanly when sessions are short-lived, leading to apparent fragmentation of the refill accounting.

Expected behavior:
- Short-lived sessions should aggregate against the tenant/api-key token bucket and not cause spiky depletion beyond real token usage.

Initial investigation notes:
- Hypothesis A: Autoscaler creates many short-lived edge runners; each runner opens a fresh local window against the rate-limiter and reserves a small token allocation. Rapid churn causes the accounting layer to treat allocations separately and not merge them quickly, causing perceived exhaustion.
- Hypothesis B: HTTP/2 connection reuse vs. new connections changes how per-connection credits are counted; short-lived connections are reconciled slowly during runner termination.
- Hypothesis C: A change in autoscaler TTL (v2.3.1) reduced runner lifetime and increased churn; older behavior allowed longer-lived allocations.

Relevant logs and links:
- Edge proxy trace: https://logs.redwood/trace/edge/trace-20260311-efd3
- Rate-limiter dashboard: https://metrics.redwood/dashboards/tenant-throttle/fjorddata-usw2
- Autoscaler rollout PR: github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/412

Workarounds found so far:
- Customer can reduce worker churn by reusing a small pool of long-lived processes (recommended immediate mitigation).
- We temporarily reverted autoscaler TTL on a canary to v2.2.x and saw reduction in 429 incidence in the canary region.

Next steps / proposed fixes:
1) Engineering to audit rate-limiter allocation logic for short-lived sessions; ensure allocations consolidate at the tenant bucket level on session termination. (Owner: rate-limiter team)
2) Add short window aggregation in accounting that merges allocations from the same api-key within a 60s reconciliation window. (Owner: runtime infra)
3) Add telemetry to surface allocation fragmentation events and correlating autoscaler churn metrics. (Owner: observability)
4) Recommend customer-facing guidance: avoid creating many short-lived API keys/processes; reuse connections where possible. (Owner: Support/Docs)

Requested from Engineering:
- Confirm whether the rate-limiter currently reserves tokens per-runner and at what time allocations are reconciled.
- Confirm if any recent PRs modified per-connection allocation behavior (search notes point to autoscaler and edge-proxy changes).

Resolution notes (pending):
- Temporary mitigation: canary rollback to autoscaler v2.2.x reduced errors; will plan for code-level fix in next sprint.
- Follow-up: patch expected in 2 sprints to perform allocation merging; document recommended patterns for dedicated customers.
